utility.notes: Ceres is a well-documented Stanislaus County city within PG&E's core Northern California service territory.

generation_supplier.notes: No Community Choice Aggregator was found serving Ceres this session.

permit_authority.notes: The City of Ceres contracts with Stanislaus County for all inspections and plan checks, per the city's own Building Code Information page.

interconnection_url.notes: PG&E's own utility-wide Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized statewide budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025 and remains an active program per SGIP's own statewide announcements (most recently dated 2026-07-23). Administered across PG&E's entire distribution territory, which includes Ceres/Stanislaus County.
value.eligibility: PG&E, SCE, or SDG&E residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Reused as a utility-level fact already established for other IOU-territory records this session: the CPUC-administered SGIP program applies uniformly across the named utility's entire distribution territory, directly verified via SGIP's own site (selfgenca.com) / the CPUC's own SGIP program page, including a program-status announcement as recent as 2026-07-23 confirming the program remains active.

value.name: Checklist of expedited-review requirements, published on the City's website

required_documents.notes: Per Ceres Municipal Code Section 15.04.040(C)(2)-(3): the building official develops a checklist of all requirements, published on the City's website; applicant submits by personal or, if available, electronic submittal.

value: Call the Building Inspections line at 209-525-6557 to request an inspection

For a small residential rooftop solar energy system eligible for expedited review, only one inspection shall be required, done in a timely manner and may include a consolidated inspection by the Building Inspector and Fire Department designee
If a small residential rooftop solar energy system fails inspection, a subsequent inspection is authorized
inspection_steps.notes: Combines the City's general Building Division inspection contact line with the solar-specific inspection provisions of Ceres Municipal Code Section 15.04.040(C)(5).

value.notes: Ceres Municipal Code Section 15.04.040(C)(7): the building official shall administratively approve the application and issue all required permits or authorizations 'within one to three working days in which the permit application is submitted.'

value.program_or_pathway: Small Residential Rooftop Solar Energy System expedited permitting (Ceres Municipal Code Section 15.04.040(C))
other_conditions: System must be installed on a single- or duplex-family dwelling
Solar panel/module array must not exceed the maximum legal building height as defined by the authority having jurisdiction
